pr.title: Fix validation on substituted callee bodies in MIR inliner
pr.description:
When inlining a coroutine, we will substitute the MIR body with the args of the call. There is code in the MIR validator that attempts to prevent query cycles, and will use the coroutine body directly when it detects that's the body that's being validated. That means that when inlining a coroutine body that has been substituted, it may no longer be parameterized over the original args of the coroutine, which will lead to substitution ICEs.

Fixes #119064

https://github.com/oxidecomputer/cancel-safe-futures on commit `857ddd3a30c5f82e6edb72ac7c8a471860501d9f`

```
RUSTFLAGS="-Zinline-mir -Zcross-crate-inline-threshold=always -Zinline-mir-hint-threshold=10000 -Zinline-mir-threshold=10000" cargo +nightly test --target=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
```
If you don't set a `--target` you will OOM while optimizing syn with these very silly flags.

```
error: internal compiler error: compiler/rustc_middle/src/ty/generic_args.rs:885:9: expected type for `T/#0` (T/#0/0) but found Lifetime(ReErased) when substituting
```
```
error: internal compiler error: compiler/rustc_middle/src/ty/generic_args.rs:885:9: expected type for `T/#0` (T/#0/0) but found Lifetime(ReErased) when substituting
```

I also have another example of this that produces a "but found Const` ICE. They look similar, I'll post the other one later if someone wants.

[rustc-ice-2023-12-18T05_32_24-344139.txt](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/files/13699738/rustc-ice-2023-12-18T05_32_24-344139.txt)

analysis.summary: The MIR validator's TypeChecker selected the coroutine body for `gen_body` based on whether the coroutine's def_id matched the body currently being validated. During MIR inlining, the callee coroutine body has already been substituted with call-site args, so it is no longer parameterized over the coroutine's original generic args. Reusing that substituted body for a coroutine-variant projection caused substitution ICEs (expected type `T` but found `Lifetime(ReErased)` or a const). The fix separates `body` (the possibly-substituted body under validation) from `caller_body` and uses `caller_body.source.def_id()` only for the query-cycle avoidance check, falling back to `optimized_mir(def_id)` otherwise.
analysis.originalLogic: In `compiler/rustc_const_eval/src/transform/validate.rs`, the TypeChecker avoided query cycles by checking `let gen_body = if def_id == self.body.source.def_id() { self.body } else { self.tcx.optimized_mir(def_id) };`. It assumed the body being validated was still the canonical, unsubstituted body for that def_id.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically wrong transformation was using `self.body` (the callee body passed to `validate_types`, already substituted with inlining call args) as `gen_body` whenever `def_id == self.body.source.def_id()`. Because the substituted inline copy is no longer parameterized over the original coroutine args, projecting a coroutine variant using that body performs substitution against mismatched generic args, producing ICEs such as `expected type for T/#0 ... but found Lifetime(ReErased) when substituting` or `but found Const`. The corrected transformation introduces `caller_body` and selects `self.caller_body` when `def_id == self.caller_body.source.def_id()`, otherwise `self.tcx.optimized_mir(def_id)`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR type validation while running the `Inline` pass on coroutine/async bodies. It applies when a callee body has been cloned and substituted with call-site arguments, then validated before inlining, and the validator encounters a `ty::Coroutine(def_id, args)` with `parent_ty.variant_index = Some(...)` (a coroutine variant field projection). Triggering programs are async fns/closures whose bodies contain coroutine construction and polling, especially with inlining thresholds forced high, cross-crate inlining, and generic/lifetime parameters in the coroutine's argument type.
analysis.trigger: Inlining a coroutine body that has been substituted with the arguments of the call. The validator sees a coroutine-variant projection whose coroutine def_id equals the substituted callee body's `source.def_id()`, and uses the substituted body as `gen_body`; generic-args substitution then fails because the body's parameterization no longer matches the original coroutine args.
preconditions: MIR inliner (`Inline`) is enabled and allowed to inline a coroutine body; issue used `-Zinline-mir -Zcross-crate-inline-threshold=always -Zinline-mir-hint-threshold=10000 -Zinline-mir-threshold=10000`.
The callee coroutine body has been substituted with the call-site args before validation.
The validator processes a coroutine variant projection (`parent_ty.variant_index` is `Some`) for a `ty::Coroutine` whose def_id matches the substituted body's source def_id.
The original coroutine is generic over types/lifetimes/consts (e.g. `ActionPermit<'_, T>` / `T`) so substitution can mismatch `Lifetime(ReErased)` or a const.
Validation occurs while `optimized_mir` for that def_id may not yet be available, which is why cycle avoidance exists.
pitfalls: Def_id equality alone does not distinguish the original coroutine body from an inlined, substituted copy; a separate `caller_body` identity is required.
Using `self.tcx.optimized_mir(def_id)` unconditionally can reintroduce a query cycle when the body being validated is the one currently being computed.
The substituted inline body must not be used as the source of coroutine generic args; only the caller/original body is parameterized over the original args.
Panic-abort and panic-unwind strategies both exhibit the same substitution issue but produce different cleanup/block structure, so expectations must be emitted per panic strategy.

`ByMoveBody` source construction in `coroutine/by_move_body.rs` was also normalized to `MirSource::from_instance`, but that refactor is not the substitution fix; do not conflate it with the validator change.
analysis.testStrategy: Use a `tests/mir-opt/` unit test for the `Inline` pass: `//@ unit-test: Inline`, `// EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY`, `// skip-filecheck`, `//@ edition: 2021`, and `//@ compile-flags: -Zinline-mir-hint-threshold=10000 -Zinline-mir-threshold=10000 --crate-type=lib`. Construct an async fn taking a generic lifetime-parameterized `ActionPermit<'_, T>` and `&mut Context`; have a generic `run2` closure create an `ActionPermit::perform(permit)` future, pin it with `Pin::new_unchecked`, and poll it. This forces coroutine-body inlining and exercises substituted callee validation. Emit `// EMIT_MIR inline_coroutine_body.run2-{closure#0}.Inline.diff` and check both panic-abort and panic-unwind diffs. The regression condition is absence of the substitution ICE and successful inlining of `ActionPermit::perform::{closure#0}`, not merely a changed MIR shape.
